function: Cascaded BS-RIS-UE channel feedback: autoencoder AE1 compresses the full channel per large timescale, AE2 compresses the per-RIS-unit variation ratio vector per small timescale (p. 2-3)
system: FDD, BS ULA with 32 antennas, passive reflecting RIS with 16x16 unit cells (UPA), single-antenna UE, direct link blocked; 2.655 GHz (band n7) (p. 2, 4)
method: Convolutional autoencoder AE1 and fully connected autoencoder AE2 with residual RefineNet blocks, 4-bit quantization, MSE loss, Adam; two-timescale feedback of channel then variation ratio; paradigm not named (p. 3-4)
data_channel: BS-RIS: Saleh-Valenzuela model with auto-regressive time variation (rho=0.9); RIS-UE: Wireless InSite ray tracing; 200,000 cascaded samples, 8:1:1 split; UE in 30x40 m area (p. 4)
test_conditions: Single scenario with 8:1:1 train/validation/test split, random UE positions at 1 m/s; sweeps over compression ratios and T=4, 9; no new scenario (p. 4-5)
baselines: Learned: Quan-Transformer feedback of [11], simplified to lightweight AE1 sent every interval; non-learned: RVQ codebook feedback, NMSE above 0 dB at 480 bits (p. 4)
metrics: NMSE (dB) averaged over the T+1 intervals versus equivalent feedback bits; performance loss; FLOPs; GPU and CPU inference time (p. 4-5)
complexity: FLOPs (Fig. 5): proposed about 1/(T+1) of baseline; inference time on GPU 0.214 ms (AE1) and 0.067 ms (AE2), on CPU 3.354 ms and 0.102 ms (p. 5)
q1_support: p. 4: "to generate BS-RIS CSI samples [19] and Wireless Insite to generate RIS-UE CSI samples [20]". Not met: the BS-RIS channel is a Saleh-Valenzuela statistical model and the RIS-UE channel a Wireless InSite run in the paper's own scenario; 3GPP TS 38.101-1 is cited only for the n7 carrier frequency.
q2_support: p. 4: "The dataset is divided into training, validation, and test sets in an 8:1:1 ratio." Not met: held-out split of one simulated scenario; the sweeps over compression ratios and T are settings of the method, with no new scenario, band, antenna or RIS size.
q3_support: p. 4: "For comparison purposes, we consider [11] as a baseline." (learned) and footnote 3: "We also consider the typical RVQ codebook-based feedback method as a baseline" (non-learned, NMSE "higher than 0 dB even when using 480 bits"); Fig. 3 (p. 5) compares NMSE with [11].
q4_support: p. 5: "In GPU settings, the inference times for AE1 and AE2 are 0.214 ms and 0.067 ms, respectively." Also "The computational complexity of the proposed method is approximately 1/(T + 1) of the baseline method" with FLOPs in Fig. 5.
q5_support: p. 4: "A total of 200,000 different cascaded channel samples are generated." Not met: data generated by the authors; no code or data link or DOI; Wireless InSite is commercial software and Saleh-Valenzuela is a statistical model.
notes: Preprint arXiv 2409.08149v1 of a TVT letter. Area 2: cascaded channel compression and feedback; the cascaded channel is assumed perfect, so channel estimation is not treated (p. 2, footnote 2). q3 caveats for the reviewer: baseline [11] is the Transformer feedback of [11] reimplemented with the authors' lightweight AE1, the same AE1 used inside the proposed method (p. 4), so it could be read as the proposed method without the ratio-vector stage; the RVQ codebook comparison is only in footnote 3 (p. 4), with no plotted curve. q1 flagged: Wireless InSite is a commercial ray tracer run in the authors' own scene, not DeepMIMO or another public dataset.
